protocol.name: adaptive_foreground

description.summary: backdrop luminance reporting for self-styling surfaces

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client ask the compositor what is behind parts of its own surface, so it can pick a foreground colour that stays legible there.
The motivating case is text drawn directly onto the wallpaper -- a desktop greeting, a widget label -- which becomes unreadable when the wallpaper's lightness happens to match the text colour the active colour scheme chose.
The compositor does not restyle the surface. It reports the relative luminance of what it composited beneath each zone the client marked, and the client restyles itself. Reporting rather than recolouring is deliberate: the client can then move text, icons, dividers and shadows together, which a compositor-side recolour of already-rasterised pixels could not do, and it needs no agreement about how those pixels were rendered.

interface.name: adaptive_foreground_manager_v1
interface.description: Grants access to per-surface backdrop luminance reporting.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager does not affect objects already created by it.

request.name: get_adaptive_foreground

description.summary: observe backdrop luminance for a surface

request.description:
Create an object that reports backdrop luminance for the given surface.
If the surface already has an adaptive_foreground_surface_v1 that has not been destroyed, the already_constructed error is raised.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has an adaptive foreground object

interface.name: adaptive_foreground_surface_v1
interface.description:
Reports the luminance of what the compositor composited beneath each zone of a surface.
A zone is a rectangle of the surface the client wants a reading for -- typically the measured bounds of a run of text. Zones are set as a wl_region and are identified in events by their index in that region, in the order the client added them.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops luminance reporting. The surface is otherwise unaffected.

request.name: set_region
request.description:
Set the zones to report luminance for, in surface-local coordinates.
Each rectangle added to the region is one zone. Zones are indexed by the order they were added, and that index is what the luminance event carries, so a client with several independently styled labels can tell their readings apart. Rectangles must be added and never subtracted; the effect of a subtract operation on the region is undefined.
A null region, or a region with no rectangles, disables reporting.
This state takes effect immediately rather than on the next wl_surface.commit. Unlike a blur region, which must land in the same frame as the surface it sits behind, a zone only says where to sample; a reading one frame stale is not observable. After the zones change the compositor sends a fresh set of luminance events for them.

event.name: luminance
event.description:
The relative luminance of what was composited beneath the zone at `index`, as a fixed-point number with 8 bits of fractional precision: 0 is black, 256 is white. It is the WCAG relative luminance of the mean colour under the zone -- a single value for the whole zone, not a gradient, because a glyph that straddles a light/dark edge reads far better in one colour than sliced into two.
Only zones whose reading actually changed are sent. A client that has received no event for a zone should keep its last value.
The compositor rate-limits these; a client must not assume it will see every intermediate value under an animated wallpaper.

event.name: done

description.summary: the current batch of readings is complete

event.description: Sent after a group of luminance events. The client should apply them together, so a surface with several zones restyles in one frame rather than one zone at a time.
